stories.headline: China Blocks Meta's $2B Acquisition of AI Startup Manus, Orders Deal Unwound

key_facts.fact: China's NDRC ordered Meta to unwind its $2 billion-plus acquisition of agentic AI startup Manus, citing violations of export controls and national security regulations.
key_facts.excerpt: China's top economic planner, the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), ordered both companies to cancel the transaction immediately. The ruling follows a months-long investigation into whether the deal violated China's strict export controls and national security regulations.

key_facts.fact: Manus became a sensation in early 2025 after releasing what it called the world's first 'general AI agent'; its core technology was developed by teams in Beijing and Wuhan before the company moved operations to Singapore.
key_facts.excerpt: Manus became a tech sensation in early 2025 after releasing what it called the world's first 'general AI agent'... While Manus is officially registered in Singapore, its roots are firmly in mainland China. The company's core technology was developed by teams in Beijing and Wuhan.

key_facts.fact: Manus co-founders were summoned to meetings with Chinese officials in March and have since been barred from leaving the country.
key_facts.excerpt: Previous reports from the Financial Times and The New York Times claimed that the co-founders of Manus were summoned to meetings with Chinese officials in March and have since been barred from leaving the country.

key_facts.fact: Beijing feared the move was a blueprint for 'technology leakage,' where homegrown Chinese AI innovation is quietly moved abroad to be acquired by American companies.
key_facts.excerpt: Beijing's regulators reportedly feared this move was a blueprint for 'technology leakage,' where homegrown Chinese innovation is quietly moved abroad to be acquired by American giants like Meta.

key_facts.fact: The block coincides with the White House issuing directives accusing China of running 'industrial-scale' efforts to steal US AI technology.
key_facts.excerpt: The White House has issued an urgent directive to government agencies, accusing China of running a massive, state-sponsored campaign to steal the American artificial intelligence (AI) technology.

stories.headline: Intellia Reports Positive Phase 3 CRISPR Results: 87% Attack Reduction, Files for FDA Approval

key_facts.fact: Lonvo-z reduced HAE attacks by 87% versus placebo in the Phase 3 HAELO trial, with a mean monthly attack rate of 0.26 vs 2.10 (p<0.0001)
key_facts.excerpt: A one-time infusion of lonvo-z reduced attacks by 87% versus placebo, with a mean monthly attack rate of 0.26 in the lonvo-z arm compared with 2.10 in the placebo arm (p<0.0001).

key_facts.fact: 62% of patients in the lonvo-z arm were entirely attack-free and therapy-free for the six-month evaluation period, versus 11% in placebo (p<0.0001)
key_facts.excerpt: A 62% rate of patients who were entirely attack free and therapy free in the lonvo-z arm for the six-month efficacy evaluation period, compared with 11% of patients in the placebo arm.

key_facts.fact: This is the first Phase 3 readout for any in vivo CRISPR gene editing therapy worldwide
key_facts.excerpt: As the first Phase 3 data reported for an in vivo gene editing therapy, today's HAELO results represent a profound milestone for Intellia, the broader CRISPR and precision medicine fields

key_facts.fact: Intellia initiated a rolling BLA submission to the FDA and anticipates U.S. launch in the first half of 2027 if approved
key_facts.excerpt: Intellia Therapeutics Initiates Rolling Submission of Biologics License Application to FDA for Lonvoguran Ziclumeran (lonvo-z) as a One-Time Treatment for Hereditary Angioedema

key_facts.fact: 80 patients were enrolled: 52 received lonvo-z and 28 placebo; all TEAEs were mild or moderate with no serious adverse events in the lonvo-z arm
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 80 patients were enrolled, with 52 receiving lonvo-z and 28 receiving placebo... All TEAEs reported as of the data cutoff were mild or moderate and there were no serious adverse events observed in the lonvo-z arm.

stories.headline: Meta Signs Deal With Overview Energy for 1GW of Space Solar Power for AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Meta signed a first-of-its-kind agreement with Overview Energy for up to 1GW of space solar energy capacity, with orbital demonstration in 2028 and commercial power delivery expected in 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Overview Energy and Meta today announced a first-of-its-kind agreement and partnership to advance American-built space solar energy with initial orbital demonstration in 2028 and commercial power delivery expected in 2030.

key_facts.fact: Overview's system collects solar energy via satellites in geosynchronous orbit and beams it as low-intensity near-infrared light to existing solar facilities on the ground, enabling around-the-clock power.
key_facts.excerpt: The system collects solar energy in space and beams it to existing solar facilities on the ground, where it is converted into electricity, allowing these assets to maximize utilization and produce power around-the-clock.

key_facts.fact: The beam is invisible, less intense than sunlight, and passively safe for humans, animals, and aircraft according to Overview.
key_facts.excerpt: Overview's beam is invisible, less intense than sunlight, and passively safe for humans, animals, and aircraft.

key_facts.fact: Meta is one of the first major companies to secure rights for future space solar energy capacity; the deal is positioned as strengthening America's energy leadership.
key_facts.excerpt: With this capacity reservation agreement, Meta is one of the first major companies to secure rights for future space solar energy capacity delivered from orbit to the grid.

key_facts.fact: Overview's advisory board includes former NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine, former NASA Administrator Mike Griffin, and former FERC Chairman Joseph Kelliher.
key_facts.excerpt: Overview's advisory board includes Jim Bridenstine, former NASA Administrator and Congressman; Mike Griffin, former NASA Administrator; and Joseph Kelliher, former FERC Chairman and EVP of Regulatory at NextEra.

stories.headline: OpenAI Publishes Five-Principle Framework for AGI, Altman Concedes Company's Larger Scale

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published a five-principle framework for AGI development on Sunday: democratization, empowerment, universal prosperity, resilience, and adaptability.
key_facts.excerpt: The post titled 'Our Principles' devotes a paragraph to each. Democratization comes first... Empowerment... Universal prosperity... Resilience pledges collaboration with companies, governments... Adaptability sits last.

key_facts.fact: Altman concedes OpenAI is 'materially larger' than at the time of the 2018 Charter and acknowledges scenarios where the company 'may have to trade off some empowerment for more resilience.'
key_facts.excerpt: He writes that OpenAI is materially larger than at the time of the 2018 Charter and acknowledges scenarios in which the company 'may have to trade off some empowerment for more resilience.' An unusual concession.

key_facts.fact: The framework is OpenAI's most prominent statement of intent since the 2018 Charter and arrives as US and European regulators tighten oversight of frontier AI labs.
key_facts.excerpt: The framework is OpenAI's most prominent statement of intent since the 2018 Charter, and arrives as U.S. and European regulators tighten oversight of frontier AI labs.

key_facts.fact: Altman writes 'We deserve an enormous amount of scrutiny given the weight of what we are doing' and commits to resisting AI technology that consolidates power 'in the hands of the few.'
key_facts.excerpt: Chief executive Sam Altman wrote in the post that the lab will 'resist the potential of this technology to consolidate power in the hands of the few.'

key_facts.fact: The post revisits OpenAI's 2019 decision to delay GPT-2 weights, calling the worry 'misplaced' but crediting it with discovering the iterative deployment strategy the company uses today.
key_facts.excerpt: The post revisits OpenAI's 2019 decision to delay the GPT-2 model weights, calling the worry 'misplaced' but crediting the episode with the discovery of iterative deployment, the company's default release strategy ever since.

key_facts.fact: Four other individuals also received jail sentences in the case

stories.headline: Taiwan Court Sentences Ex-Tokyo Electron Engineer to 10 Years for TSMC Trade Secret Theft

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's Intellectual Property and Commercial Court sentenced former Tokyo Electron engineer Chen Li-ming to 10 years in prison for stealing TSMC's proprietary data
key_facts.excerpt: A Taiwanese court has sentenced a former Tokyo Electron employee to 10 years in prison for stealing Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.'s (TSMC) proprietary data

key_facts.fact: Four others indicted received sentences of up to six years; one woman got a 10-month suspended sentence
key_facts.excerpt: Four others indicted in the case were given sentences of as much as six years in prison, with one woman getting a 10-month sentence, suspended for three years.

key_facts.fact: Tokyo Electron's Taiwan unit was fined NT$150 million ($4.8 million) and ordered to pay NT$100 million to TSMC
key_facts.excerpt: The court also fined Tokyo Electron's Taiwan unit 150 million New Taiwan dollars ($4.8 million) and ordered NT$100 million to be paid to TSMC.

key_facts.fact: Chen did not leak trade secrets beyond Tokyo Electron and its Taiwan unit; the judge said the company could have done more to monitor employees
key_facts.excerpt: Chen did not leak trade secrets to outside parties beyond Tokyo Electron and its Taiwan unit... But the Japanese company could have done more to monitor its employees, the judge said.

key_facts.fact: Tokyo Electron said it takes the court's finding 'with utmost seriousness' and has had discussions with TSMC to better protect trade secrets
key_facts.excerpt: Tokyo Electron said in a statement it takes the court's finding 'with utmost seriousness.' The company has had discussions with TSMC to come up with ways to better protect trade secrets and confidential information

stories.headline: Tokyo Electron Cuts Ties With Veteran China Exec After Discovering Family Investments in Rival Chipmakers

key_facts.fact: Tokyo Electron severed ties with Jay Chen, who led the company's China operations, after discovering his family-linked investment structures were connected to Chinese chip start-ups developing competing tools
key_facts.excerpt: Tokyo Electron has severed ties with a veteran executive after an investigation uncovered alleged connections to Chinese chip start-ups linked to emerging competitors.

key_facts.fact: One of the start-ups linked to Chen transitioned from servicing Tokyo Electron equipment to developing competing chipmaking tools
key_facts.excerpt: Chen's family-linked investment structures were associated with Chinese start-ups, including one that transitioned from servicing Tokyo Electron equipment to developing competing chipmaking tools.

key_facts.fact: Tokyo Electron became aware of the investment connections in late 2024, replaced Chen in early 2025, and later retained him temporarily as a special adviser before his contract expired
key_facts.excerpt: The company confirmed that it became aware of the investment connections in late 2024 and subsequently replaced Chen in early 2025, later retaining him temporarily as a special adviser before his contract expired.

key_facts.fact: Tokyo Electron is a dominant supplier of semiconductor manufacturing tools, holding a leading global position in 'track systems' essential to the lithography process
key_facts.excerpt: Tokyo Electron is a dominant supplier in the semiconductor manufacturing industry, providing critical tools used by major chipmakers such as TSMC, Samsung, and Intel. It holds a leading global position in 'track systems.'
